newsitem.title: USA: US gives airlines rights to fly cargo to Thailand.
newsitem.headline: US gives airlines rights to fly cargo to Thailand.

text.p: The U.S. Department of Transportation said it granted five airlines the rights to provide scheduled cargo flight service to Thailand under a pact worked out earlier this year.
The department awarded the flight authority as follows: United Parcel Service, six weekly flights; Air Micronesia, five; Federal Express, five; Northwest Airlines, three; and Polar Air Cargo, two.
U.S. and Thai negotiators reached an agreement in January that provided for greatly expanded service opportunities for the airlines of both countries.

"These new U.S.-carrier services will significantly expand options for shippers in the U.S.-Thailand market as well as stimulate trade between our nations," Transportation Secretary Federico Pena said in a statement.
The department confirmed an earlier grant of three additional weekly all-cargo flights to Thailand -- two to Northwest and one to Federal Express.
